dedupe_keys.name: dynamic probabilistic material flow analysis of seven polymers in europe 1950 2016 empa

description: This data set traces how seven common plastics have flowed through the European economy from 1950 to 2016, from production and use in products to collection, recycling, incineration, landfill and export. The producers are Delphine Kawecki, Qie Wu and Bernd Nowack of Empa, the Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology, with João Gonçalves of the University of Zurich. It is a dynamic probabilistic material flow analysis covering low and high density polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, expanded polystyrene, PVC and PET across nine product sectors and 35 product categories, including textiles; consumption of these polymers reached about 90 kilograms per person in 2016, and landfill is the largest end compartment. Each of the roughly 1,200 files gives the Monte Carlo distribution of one flow between two compartments, such as electrical equipment to mixed waste collection or end-of-life vehicle collection to shredder residue recycling. The files are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: continental totals without national or facility detail, many parameters are estimated, and file names are the main documentation. Simulation uses: estimating plastic waste arriving at collection, sorting and treatment infrastructure, and testing recycling capacity scenarios. Related records: ODYM (model-odym) is a material flow modelling framework, and the Eurostat municipal waste statistics (data-eurostat-env-wasmun) report treatment by country.
name: Dynamic probabilistic material flow analysis of seven polymers in Europe, 1950-2016 (Empa)
provider: Delphine Kawecki, Qie Wu, Bernd Nowack (Empa, Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology) and João S. V. Gonçalves (University of Zurich)
schema_summary: About 1,200 CSV files of logged Monte Carlo outflows between compartments for LDPE, HDPE, PP, PS, EPS, PVC and PET: from product sectors (such as automotive, building and construction, electrical and electronic equipment) through collection (mixed waste, end-of-life vehicles) to recycling, incineration, landfill and export
